title.value: Emerging Bronchoscopic Therapies for Lung Disease: Targeted Lung Denervation, Rheoplasty, and Spray Cryotherapy

key_points: Targeted lung denervation (TLD) ablates parasympathetic vagal fibers with radiofrequency to reduce bronchoconstriction and exacerbations in COPD.
Bronchial rheoplasty applies non-thermal pulsed electrical energy to ablate goblet cells and reduce sputum burden in chronic bronchitis.
Spray cryotherapy delivers metered liquid nitrogen at approximately −196 °C to ablate abnormal mucosa and reduce mucus hypersecretion.
Careful phenotype-based selection is essential: TLD for frequent exacerbators; rheoplasty and spray cryotherapy for chronic bronchitis with high symptom burden.
Preprocedure CT is required for TLD to assess bronchial anatomy and exclude severe emphysema (emphysema index >50% at −950 HU).

clinical_procedures.name: Targeted Lung Denervation (TLD)
steps: General anesthesia; insert dual-cooled radiofrequency catheter via bronchoscope.
Position catheter circumferentially in each main bronchus to ablate vagal fibers at four positions.
Use esophageal balloon with contrast to maintain distance from esophagus and avoid gastric vagal ablation.
Energy selection based on anatomy (26–32 W); radiofrequency activation for 120 s followed by 30 s postcooling.
Administer prophylactic antibiotics and corticosteroids; typical total procedure time ≈74 min.
notes: Possible adverse events: COPD exacerbation, pulmonary infection, airway mucosal damage, gastrointestinal side effects.

clinical_procedures.name: Bronchial Rheoplasty
steps: Under general anesthesia, perform two sessions: right lung then 4–6 weeks later left lung.
Deploy catheter in subsegmental bronchi and advance proximally toward main carina, treating each segment.
Expand electrode to contact mucosa; apply current for 5 s per activation; collapse and move to next site.
Typical duration ≈40 min with ~40–60 activations per side; administer corticosteroids to reduce COPD exacerbation risk.
notes: Contraindicated with cardiac arrhythmias or implantable electronic devices due to timing to heart rhythm and monopolar electrode.

clinical_procedures.name: Spray Cryotherapy (Metered Cryospray)
steps: Insert delivery catheter through bronchoscope; connect to liquid-nitrogen console.
Deliver liquid nitrogen as radial spray with thermocouple feedback to create an ≈10 mm circular ablation zone (depth 0.1–0.5 mm).
Stop ventilation during application and usually deflate endotracheal tube cuff to avoid barotrauma or asphyxia.
Perform three procedures: (1) right lower lobe + right mainstem, (2) left lower lobe + left mainstem, (3) both upper lobes + distal trachea; do not treat right middle lobe.
Mean number of sprays ≈20 per procedure; mean procedure time ≈34 min.
notes: Evidence shows mucosal/submucosal effect without cartilage injury in pilot studies.
Main adverse events: COPD exacerbations and pneumonia; no pneumothorax reported in cited series.

treatment_algorithms.title: Phenotype-based selection for bronchoscopic COPD therapies

specific_recommendations.text: Ensure symptoms persist despite optimized medical and conservative therapy.
If emphysema phenotype with hyperinflation: consider lung volume reduction (endoscopic or surgical).
If frequent exacerbations (≥2 moderate in last 12 months requiring antibiotics or corticosteroids): consider TLD.
If chronic bronchitis with CAT sputum+cough ≥7 and total ≥10: consider bronchial rheoplasty or spray cryotherapy.

clinical_guidelines.title: TLD selection and peri-procedural guidance
specific_recommendations: Select patients with ≥2 moderate exacerbations in prior 12 months on optimal therapy.
Exclude asthma, persistent bacterial colonization, and significant gastrointestinal comorbidities.
Obtain CT to exclude severe emphysema (emphysema index >50% at −950 HU).
Use esophageal balloon to maintain distance from esophagus during ablation.

clinical_guidelines.title: Rheoplasty selection and technique
specific_recommendations: Use CAT thresholds (first two questions ≥7; total ≥10) to define high symptom burden.
Exclude emphysema index >25% at −950 HU, asthma bronchiale, and known colonization with resistant organisms (e.g., Pseudomonas).
Avoid in cardiac arrhythmias or with implantable electronic devices.

clinical_guidelines.title: Spray cryotherapy selection and technique
specific_recommendations: Eligible if chronic bronchitis + COPD for ≥2 years; exclude asthma or bronchiectasis.
Plan three staged procedures; do not treat right middle lobe due to barotrauma risk.
Stop ventilation and usually deflate cuff during applications.

definitions.definition: Targeted lung denervation; RF ablation of parasympathetic vagal fibers to reduce bronchoconstriction and exacerbations.
Non-thermal pulsed electrical ablation of goblet cells to reduce sputum burden in chronic bronchitis.
Delivery of liquid nitrogen at approximately −196 °C to ablate abnormal mucosa with limited depth.
COPD Assessment Test; used here with thresholds for CB symptom burden (first two questions ≥7; total ≥10).
St. George’s Respiratory Questionnaire; symptom score used in COPD studies.
Leicester Cough Questionnaire; cough-related symptom score.
CT-based percentage of lung voxels below −950 HU; thresholds >50% (TLD exclusion) and >25% (rheoplasty exclusion).

clinical_pearls: Phenotype first: emphysema → consider lung volume reduction; frequent exacerbations → TLD; chronic bronchitis → rheoplasty or cryospray.
Use CT to assess anatomy and emphysema burden before TLD; exclude severe emphysema.
For rheoplasty, manage oxygen (FiO2 ≈30%) during activations and anticipate COPD exacerbations post-procedure.
During cryospray, stop ventilation and usually deflate the cuff to avoid barotrauma; avoid treating right middle lobe.

clinical_applications: Offer TLD to frequent COPD exacerbators despite optimal therapy, after exclusion criteria and CT review.
Consider rheoplasty or metered cryospray for chronic bronchitis with high symptom burden when standard care is insufficient.
practice_recommendations: Use standardized selection thresholds (exacerbations; CAT; emphysema index).
Adhere to device-specific safety steps (esophageal balloon for TLD; FiO2 reduction for rheoplasty; ventilation pause for cryospray).
future_directions: Confirm long-term efficacy and safety in randomized trials (e.g., AIRFLOW-3; sham-controlled studies for rheoplasty and cryospray).
Define retreatment criteria for rheoplasty and durability of cryospray benefits.
controversies: Optimal thresholds for emphysema index and CAT scoring across devices.
Generalizability beyond specialized centers; reimbursement barriers.

technology_and_technique.summary: Dual-cooled RF catheter with peristaltic pump circulates coolant to limit bronchial injury; esophageal balloon increases safety margin.
Non-thermal pulsed electrical energy induces goblet-cell apoptosis with extracellular matrix preservation.
Liquid nitrogen dosing guided by thermocouple feedback to achieve target ablation diameter and depth.

points: COPD phenotypes benefit from differentiated bronchoscopic options beyond lung volume reduction.
TLD targets frequent exacerbations; rheoplasty and cryospray target chronic bronchitis symptoms.
Early studies show feasibility and symptom improvement; larger randomized trials are needed before routine use.
